pairs.difference: A (neck pillow): the light comes from the upper left. The right and lower lobes turn smoothly into a deeper violet shadow, with a pinkish bounce along the bottom edge. This matches the soft side-lit modelling on the beach ball. B (sheriff star): lit almost straight on with low light bias (0.159). The star's flat faces and ball tips carry the same even brightness, with only a thin darker rim on the lower edges and no clear shadow side.
pairs.fix: Light the star from the upper left. Make the right and lower bevels of each point clearly darker, and give each ball tip one small soft highlight on the upper left with a darker underside.

pairs.difference: A (harmonica): a strong key from the upper left. There is a broad soft sheen on the top cover, and the front face and right end fall into shadow. B (folding fan): the light/dark alternation on the pleats is mostly paper colour, not light. The lens shows almost no form turn (form contrast 0.213, below the real range). There is no shadow under the ribs or the handle and no cast shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the fan from the upper left. Shade each pleat so its far side turns darker, put a soft shadow under the ribs where they meet the handle, and add a faint shadow of the fan on the background.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): the light comes from the upper left. The right sleeve, the hem and the inside of the collar go into deep, cool shadow, and the folds turn gradually. B (cowboy hat): even, smooth plastic shading. A bright rim glow runs all along the brim edge, and the crown has very little difference between its lit and shadow sides. The shading range (0.843) is above the real range.
pairs.fix: Remove the glowing outline on the brim. Light the hat from the upper left so the right side of the crown and the underside of the brim fall into a clear, darker shadow, and put a soft shadow under the band.

pairs.difference: A (caravan): the key is from the front left. The right side panel falls into a cool blue shadow, as on the real camera and computer, and there is contact shadow under the chassis. B (buoy): stacked cylinders with soft, even grey shading and only a mild darkening on the right. Form contrast (0.355) is below the real range. There is little contact darkening where the buoy meets the water.
pairs.fix: Light the buoy from the left so the right half of each cylinder turns into a clearly darker, slightly cool shadow. Darken the underside of each ledge, and darken the base where it touches the water.

pairs.difference: A (sneakers): flat frontal light, with light bias (0.019) below the real range. Both shoes are lit almost equally, and a hard dark cast shadow sits on the floor to the left. B (boots): a side key with a darker far boot and darker shaft interiors. The shading is soft and wraps around the toes, with a soft floor shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the sneakers from the upper right so the left sides of both shoes and the far shoe sit in softer shadow. Make the floor shadow softer and lighter at its edges.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): backlit by the radial rays. The ribs carry a similar mid-dark value all round, and form contrast (0.352) is below the real range. A long cast shadow lies to the left. B (spring duck): a clear upper-left key, with soft highlights on the head and wing, a shadowed belly, and contact shadow under the base.
pairs.fix: Light the cactus from the upper right. Give each rib a bright lit edge and a darker groove, darken the right sides of the arms, and add contact darkening where the trunk enters the sand.

pairs.difference: A (bandana): soft wraparound light with light bias (0.056) below the real range. The fabric folds sit in nearly the same grey, and there is no shadow side or cast shadow. B (grad cap): the board's top face is lit, the skull cap underneath falls into a deep shadow, and the tassel has a lit side and a dark side.
pairs.fix: Light the bandana from the upper left. Put the inside of the neck loop and the lower right of the triangle in a clearly darker shadow, and shade the knot so its underside is dark.

pairs.difference: A (boxing gloves): a top-left key with soft rounded form turn, and contact shadow on the wood under both gloves. B (saddle): a side key, with a darker flap under the seat and a crisp metal stirrup. Both cards are plausible on lighting.

A (rocking chair): a left key. The rails and spindles turn gradually, and the soft cast shadows on the floorboards follow the rockers. B (covered wagon): strong left light with light bias (0.91) at the top of the real range. The canvas and wheels have simple two-step shading, and there is a heavy vignette around the scene.
pairs.fix: Soften the light on the wagon. Let the canvas roll turn gradually from a lit top to a shadowed lower right, and give the wheels a softer shadow side with a gentle contact shadow on the dirt.

pairs.difference: B (lighthouse) is the known real card from the lessons: the left side of the tower is in cool shadow and the lantern glows. A (windmill): warm frontal light with light bias (0.71) above the real range. The tower faces are lit almost evenly, the wheel blades all have the same value, and a long cast shadow lies across the grass.
pairs.fix: Light the windmill tower from the side so one face falls into a clearly darker, cool shadow. Shade the wheel blades so the far ones are darker, and shorten and soften the shadow on the grass.

pairs.difference: A (campfire): the fire is a practical light that throws a believable warm glow onto the logs, stones and kettle, with dark undersides. B (tourist binoculars): uniform glossy blue plastic. Form contrast (0.627) is above the real range, with crisp dark undersides on the eyepieces and the post, and no environment bounce from the bright sky.
pairs.fix: Light the binocular viewer softly from the sky behind it. Add a pale rim along the top edges, use a gentler shadow under the eyepieces, and let some cool light bounce up into the shadows from the balcony.

pairs.difference: A (phone booth): side light. The left face is darker than the right, and the base has contact shadow. B (trophy): a top spotlight, with sheen on the gold cup and contact shadow on the table. Both cards fall within the real ranges and both are plausible.

pattern: Generated cards light the hero almost head-on or with soft wraparound light, so they lack the clear cool shadow side that real cards have (on the real camera and computer, one whole face falls into a blue-grey shadow). Their forms either turn in flat two-step bands or barely turn at all. Some add an even glowing rim around the silhouette, or a long hard cast shadow, in place of soft contact darkening.
